chapter: With the Goldkette band: Bix and Trumbauer
title: Waiting for tunes, learning to score and the Roseland debut
summary: Challis admits he did not know what scoring was, while the band waited for hit tunes and then impressed Roseland audiences.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: MR. CHALLIS: So did Donald Murray. Well, so the band had those arrangements, but actually for nice tunes, pop tunes, they didn't have too many, and they were interested -- the band had always felt that it hadn't had any hits, recorded hits so they were sort of -- I was sort of lying back until they got the arrangements. They went down to New York and they were going to get the tunes to do and that would give me about a week or two weeks, ten days, something like that, to work on some of the tunes.

One of the first things, he says, he asked me, 'Do you score?' I thought, 'What the hell's he talking about? Asking me. Score, you get score paper, and you write it down,' and he explained it to me and I said, 'Oh, I just write out the parts and that's it.' So 'Well, we'll have to get you some score paper' and I didn't know too much and it's naive or stupid to say that. But at that time, I hadn't scored, I didn't know what scoring was all about. The only way to make an arrangement, I thought, was write out the parts and if you made a mistake, you could go back and look it over on the part. So anyway they had some

score paper around there and -- but there was nothing much that I could do except wait for him to come back with these tunes, which of course he never did. We got down into New York. I don't know what I did at that time but it really wasn't too much. But I did go out and listen to the band and got acquainted with the band and I must have done one or two things there, because we hadn't enough things to play, that is, we had a few things to play when we got into the Roseland. But we went in there, the first time we were in there, geez we really sort of knocked them cold. They didn't expect a band like that. Any band with Trumbauer and Bix in it is going to be Fantastic. And Murray and the other guys who were in it also.
